# Pinned Core 2.0 Inputs

This is the complete recursive `test/core` WAST inventory, including `simd`,
from WebAssembly/spec commit `fffc6e12fa454e475455a7b58d3b5dc343980c10`
(`wg-2.0`). WABT `wast2json` 1.0.41 at
`03a00a1334e6121fb0cce4fccbd6bb109b68acaa` produces binary modules and JSON
script commands. Its `--no-check` option preserves invalid modules for the VM
to reject; it does not remove negative assertions.

| Inventory | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| WAST scripts, including SIMD | 148 |
| Script commands | 54,006 |
| Binary execution/validation/linking assertions | 51,139 |
| WAT text-parser malformed assertions | 1,091 |
| Generated fixture files, including two license notices | 5,822 |

The binary assertions include 45,734 expected returns, 2,408 traps, 2,146
invalid modules, 719 malformed binaries, 83 linking failures, 34 instantiation
failures and 15 exhaustion assertions. The remaining commands define 1,599
modules, perform 155 actions, and register 22 module names.

**These are prepared inputs, not VM passes.** M1 has not implemented module
decoding, validation or execution. Its acceptance target is every binary
assertion above and its prerequisite commands, on both host compilers and
platforms. The 1,091 text-parser assertions remain in the inventory and
generated files as a separate classification: WAT syntax parsing belongs to
the pinned development producer and is outside the binary VM API. Their
preparation does not claim a successful malformed-text assertion run either.

## Generate and verify

From the repository root, with Python 3.11 or newer:

```sh
python3 scripts/core2_corpus.py
python3 scripts/core2_corpus.py --verify-only
```

The first command downloads checksum- and size-pinned source/tool archives,
extracts the complete WAST inventory, converts every script, and compares all
generated bytes and counts with the committed records. Fixtures live under
the ignored `artifacts/core2/fixtures` directory. A subsequent invocation
verifies existing fixtures instead of replacing them. A corrupt, missing or
extra file, failed download, unsupported producer platform, conversion error,
or count mismatch is a failure, never a skip.

`pins.json` identifies the exact input archive, producer commit/version,
arguments and Linux amd64/macOS arm64 release assets. `manifest.json` records
source-file hashes, script identities and command/assertion counts.
`files.sha256` covers every generated JSON/Wasm/WAT file and license notice.
Both platforms must reproduce the same files; compiler-specific subsets are
not permitted. CI retains `artifacts/core2/evidence.json`, which records the
actual producer executable hash and input/output identities. LLVM/Go are not
involved in WAST conversion, and a conversion result is separate from guest
execution.

## Update through a PR

Change the input pins deliberately and generate into a fresh output directory:

```sh
python3 scripts/core2_corpus.py --output artifacts/core2-update --update-manifest
```

Review changed source inventories, command classifications, generated hashes
and notices. Then regenerate normally on both supported platforms and rerun
all affected VM tests before accepting a new conformance baseline. The update
flag is not used by CI; CI cannot bless changed outputs by rewriting records.

## Provenance and notices

The source archive is
[`WebAssembly/spec` at the pinned revision](https://github.com/WebAssembly/spec/tree/fffc6e12fa454e475455a7b58d3b5dc343980c10/test/core).
The producer is
[`WebAssembly/wabt` 1.0.41](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wabt/releases/tag/1.0.41).
Their archive digests are recorded in `pins.json`.

`LICENSE.spec` preserves the source repository's directory-specific notice;
`LICENSE.tests` preserves the Apache-2.0 terms applying to `test/`. Generated
test inputs derive from those tests and retain both notices. No upstream VM
implementation is copied here, and these notices do not select a license for
wasmvm's own code.
